newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere shares jump on Thomson wim.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere shares jump on Thomson wim.

text.p: Shares in French conglomerate Lagardere Groupe requoted at 170 francs per share on Thursday, after being suspended limit up at several successive attempts to trade during the morning.

The shares closed on Tuesday at 133.10 francs and were suspended on Wednesday as the French government announced Lagardere was its preferred bidder in the privatisation of electronics group Thomson SA.
Lagardere stock was up 25.17 percent at 166.6 francs at 1012 GMT, on turnover of 2.2 million shares.

Investors piled into Lagardere, whose interests span missiles firm Matra to book publisher Hachette, at the market opening, bidding the price above the 15 percent trading limit set by the SBF stock markets association.
The stock eventually resumed trading after the SBF set an upper trading limit of 204 francs per share, up from an earlier 161.30 francs.
Lagardere stands to gain the Thomson-CSF defence electronics company, on what the market sees as highly advantageous terms, if the government confirms its sale of the Thomson SA parent to Lagardere.

Merging Matra with Thomson-CSF would create a French defence group with 60 billion francs of annual sales and marry Thomson's radar and telecommunications skills with Matra's missiles and satellites, making a world scale player to compete with U.S. giants.
Lagardere was bidding against engineering group Alcatel Alsthom. Alcatel shares fell 0.26 percent to 454.50 francs.
Thomson-CSF traded down 1.24 percent to 159.20 francs from Tuesday's close. The stock was also suspended on Wednesday.
